limits: Six deliberately adversarial authored controls, not a representative sample.
Expected labels and before-P labels are author judgments; no native-human or audio evaluation.
Only candidate English/te/actualtts and empty context are sent, never expected labels, deterministic outputs or before wordings.
Two replies do not establish reviewer reliability, independence of model errors, or a production improvement.
English maps are empty so te==actualtts; this does not exercise Latin substitution errors.
No speed comparison or automatic policy adoption.

independent_text_audit.reviewer: Separate assistant agent; not a native-human evaluation
caveats: Case2 Telugu deadline can be read as by noon rather than strict before noon; ordinary intended deadline is preserved, but boundary nuance remains.
Case4 also adds the discourse word also; the material negation reversal remains explicit.
Synthetic prior P labels establish the tested precondition; they were not freshly obtained from the production reviewer.

conclusion: Supports the known length-proxy failure mechanism on these six authored controls. Does not establish semantic-review accuracy on real jobs or justify a production policy change.
interpretation_note: Case 2 has an unresolved before-noon/by-noon boundary nuance; six matches to authored labels must not be presented as six independently proven correct judgments. The clear shorter-date repair and four defective controls demonstrate the mechanism without relying on that case.
